chapter: Hartwick and the CBS staff years
title: The closed circle of New York studio musicians
summary: A select group of three or four hundred musicians did most of the work, fewer than a third jazz players; staff names including Specs Powell.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Of this body of musicians that you are working with over this period, was there a relatively stable court musician that you were around? Was it a relatively hard group to get into?

Well, it was relatively difficult. You know, that is the person that I heard when I got to New York. They said it was one of the choice jobs in town and it was very difficult yet into. It was a small group of musicians. Most of them were also the musicians that also did the books of recording. They did both jazz, and, you know… When you walk into studio recording for singers.

Well, jingles, there were a lot of jingle dates. But, all of these musicians where sort of a select group. A lot of them were on staff at the various studios, besides, they did freelance recording. So, it was a closed group. I would say maybe three or 400 musicians and they did the bulk of all of the work.
Of this body of musicians, how many of them were jazz musicians?
A relatively small number of jazz musicians. I would say less than a third.
Can you give us some names of people you worked with during your tenure in that world? Or people who were active and prominent?

Well, I mentioned some names like Jimmy Nottingham and Joe Waller. Ernie Rall was on staff at ABC. You might know Ernie Rall, his brother worked with Basie’s band. Sad and I worked it CBS Specs Powell worked at CBS for eight years. You know, CBS had people on staff like Ben Webster, Teddy Wilson, people like that. They all quit because they could not make enough money on staff. But, long before we started on staff they had been there. But, there were people like that and some other names. Probably, not well known names, but they were there.
Well, give us some not well-known names.
They’re not well known because I can't remember them! (Laughs.)
I can't think of a better reason than that! (Laughs)
